newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI shares drop after merger changes.
newsitem.headline: QNI shares drop after merger changes.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer QNI Ltd fell almost three percent after reinstatement to trading following the annoucement that it was changing some of its merger terms with Gencor Ltd's nickel unit.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), QNI shares were 10 cents or about four percent lower at A$2.40, on turnover of 257,249 shares.

Under the deal, QNI will issue 455.8 million new shares to Gencor's base metals arm Billiton Plc, representing 52.5 percent of the enlarged QNI. The capital return to shareholders would be 30 cents per share, compared with 28 cents previously.
The original merger proposal was for the issue of 504 million QNI shares to Gencor, which would have given the South African-based group a 55 percent stake in the enlarged group.
"The market has obviously taken it very badly," said one Brisbane based broker.
